checks.detail: K(4) degrees [4]; S~_4 cell degrees [4] (both = 4, so the two graphs have the same degree -- a necessary condition for cospectrality of regular graphs)
girth K(4) = 6 inside the radius-3 ball (|B_3| = 41), and mu_r = 6 <= 2r = 6, so the ball-internal value IS the girth (a shortest cycle through the root has all vertices within distance girth/2)
girth S~_4 = 4 inside the radius-2 ball (|B_2| = 15); mu_r = 4 <= 2r = 4. For m >= 4 the Coxeter diagram is a cycle, so s_1 and s_3 are non-adjacent and commute: 1, s_1, s_1 s_3, s_3 is a 4-cycle
girth K(4) = 6 != girth S~_4 = 4. A graph isomorphism preserves girth, so the two graphs are NOT isomorphic. This step is fully elementary and does not depend on any quoted theorem.

Q^v = {lam in Z^4 : sum(lam) = 0} is cut out by 1 independent equation(s) (the single row of ones, rank 1), so rank Q^v = 4 - 1 = 3. mQ^v is a finite-index sublattice of Q^v, hence the same rank. K(4) has period lattice mQ^v and S~_4 has Q^v, so both have periodic rank 3

Spec K(4): chi = 1 gives exactly {-4, +4}; over a 216-point grid every |S(chi)| <= 4. The PROOF that the whole interval [-4, 4] is attained is the paper's section 3; these numbers are a cross-check, not the proof

the paper's section 6 says a finite computation on the cell separates the pair 'if and only if the two cells are not isomorphic as voltage graphs'. Here |V(cell_K)| = 2 != 24 = m! = |V(cell_S~_4)|, so they are separated trivially (the count differs before any search is needed)
